slides.heading: Multi String Search
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Tries
slides.narration: Let's solve Multi String Search, a hard tries problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: For each small string, does it occur in the big string?
Trie of small strings, scanned from every start position of the big string.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. For each small string, does it occur in the big string? Trie of small strings, scanned from every start position of the big string.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Put the small strings in a trie, then walk it from each position of the big string.
slides.narration: Put the small strings in a trie, then walk it from each position of the big string.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: indexOf per small string → O(b · Σs)
Trie of smalls, walk from each index of big → O(b · maxS + Σs)
slides.narration: Searching for each small string separately repeats scans. A trie of the small strings lets each start index check all of them at once. Aho-Corasick makes it linear.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Start a walk at each index of the big string
slides.narration: Step by step. First, build a trie. Second, start a walk at each index of the big string. Third, mark words found. Fourth, return booleans.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We build a trie with words at terminal nodes. For each start index, follow children while they exist, adding words. Then map each small to whether it was found.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: O(ns + bs) where b is the big length, s the longest small
slides.narration: Time is O of ns plus bs where b is the big length, s the longest small. Space is O of ns.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Duplicates and overlaps are handled naturally by the set of found words.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Mention Aho-Corasick for true linear time.
